peerSolutions.title: Python centered pyramid from row lists
peerSolutions.author: Priya Verma
peerSolutions.content:
Here the current row is assembled as a list of characters and then joined before printing. The list makes the two sections of the row clear: padding first, then the stars.

```python
class Solution:
    def pattern7(self, n):
        for row in range(1, n + 1):
            line = []
            line.extend([" "] * (n - row))
            line.extend(["*"] * (2 * row - 1))
            print("".join(line))
```

The pattern stays centered because the number of spaces drops by one whenever the row number increases. At the same time, two stars are added to the row.

The list is rebuilt for every row, so no complete pattern is kept in memory. An empty or negative size simply produces no lines.

Time complexity: `O(n^2)`.
Space complexity: `O(n)` for the list representing one row.

peerSolutions.title: Python rows built with string multiplication
peerSolutions.author: Aishwarya Iyer
peerSolutions.content:
Each line can be made directly as two strings. One string contains the leading spaces, and the other contains the odd number of stars for that row. This keeps the code short without storing the whole pattern.

```python
class Solution:
    def pattern7(self, n):
        for row in range(1, n + 1):
            spaces = " " * (n - row)
            stars = "*" * (2 * row - 1)
            print(spaces + stars)
```

The star count is always odd: `1, 3, 5, ...`. For `n = 4`, the last row has seven stars and no leading spaces.

The method handles `n <= 0` by printing no rows. It only creates the current line, so the input is left unchanged.

Time complexity: `O(n^2)`.
Space complexity: `O(n)` for the current row string.
